small_guidance:
- The fused clamp/div tail is tiny relative to the ConvTranspose3d (which dominates at ~100ms). Tuning BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps on the elementwise kernel will not move the needle; only kernel-level conv changes will.
- If staying with cuDNN, try disabling channels_last_3d (cuDNN ConvTranspose3d often has no optimized NDHWC kernel and falls back to slow path) and re-benchmark with `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` in plain NCDHW.
- Ensure the bias add from ConvTranspose3d is absorbed into the fused epilogue (currently the bias add is a separate cuDNN epilogue) — fold bias into the clamp/div kernel.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile) computing the input×kernel outer product and scattering into the output grid with stride=2, padding=1, kernel=3. Fuse bias + clamp(min=-1) + multiply by (1/divisor) into the epilogue so the output is written once.
- Equivalently, formulate as a gather-style GEMM: for each output voxel (od,oh,ow) iterate over the 3×3×3 kernel taps whose corresponding input index `(od+pad - kd)/stride` is integral and in-range; this avoids atomics. Tile over OC (BLOCK_N=64) and output spatial (BLOCK_M=64), reduce over IC*valid-taps (BLOCK_K=32), autotune num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}.
- Use NDHWC layout for both input and weight (reorder weight once in __init__ to [kd,kh,kw,IC,OC]) so the K-dim reduction over IC is contiguous and coalesced; precompute the per-output list of valid kernel taps via constexpr branches on (od+pad)%stride.
